title: Gucci Bloom vs Gucci Guilty: Which Should You Wear?
summary: Gucci Bloom vs Gucci Guilty Pour Femme: a green white floral against a warm amber fougere. Compare notes, longevity, and best occasions on Scentbird.
body_markdown:
Two Gucci women’s fragrances end up in the same shopping cart more often than any other pair from the brand, yet they barely share a single chord.[Gucci Bloom](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/gucci-gucci-bloom-1427) is built entirely out of white flowers left to speak for themselves, while[Gucci Guilty Pour Femme](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/gucci-guilty-pour-femme-1429) borrows the fern-and-amber skeleton of a men’s fougere and dresses it in peach and lilac. The Gucci Bloom vs Gucci Guilty question is really a question about which shape of perfume suits you, a bouquet or a structured accord, and that answer tends to be obvious once you know what to smell for.


Gucci Bloom, available on Scentbird.


## Gucci Bloom vs Gucci Guilty: what they share


Both are Gucci women’s Eau de Parfum releases built around one defining accord rather than a wide, generic bouquet: Bloom leans entirely on tuberose and jasmine, Guilty Pour Femme leans entirely on its geranium fougere. Both also skip the safe, watered-down middle ground of mainstream florals, so neither one disappears into a crowded room, and both have earned genuinely divided fan bases because of it. Neither leans on a bright citrus overture the way so many mainstream releases do, which is part of why both smell distinct on a store shelf full of similar bottles. If you tend to like fragrances with a clear point of view, either bottle will reward that.


## Gucci Bloom


Alberto Morillas composed Gucci Bloom for the brand in 2017 around tuberose and jasmine sambac, then added Rangoon creeper, a climbing flower that shifts color as it opens, to keep the bouquet from turning candied. The result smells closer to a cut stem in a glass of cold water than to a bottled perfume counter floral, with a faint powdery edge instead of sweetness. Expect a bold first impression that tapers within an hour or two into something that sits close to the skin, with total wear typically landing between seven and nine hours. Its narrowness is also the catch: because there is no citrus or fruit to soften the transition, anyone who doesn’t already respond to tuberose has nowhere else in the composition to hide. Skip it if you’d rather ease into a floral through fruit or citrus first.


## Gucci Guilty Pour Femme


Gucci Guilty Pour Femme starts from an unusual place for a women’s perfume: a fougere accord, the fern-and-lavender skeleton normally reserved for men’s fragrances, built here around geranium instead. Aurelien Guichard composed it for Gucci in 2010, opening on pink pepper, mandarin, and black currant before geranium and lilac take over the heart, then closing on amber, patchouli, and vanilla. That base is where most of the wear time lives, holding for roughly seven to nine hours with sillage strongest through the first stretch after application. Because the drydown leans so hard on amber and patchouli, it can read heavier and more mature than the peach-lilac opening suggests, without much cool or green relief anywhere in the structure to balance it. Skip it if you want a floral that stays light and linear from open to close.


## Gucci Bloom vs Gucci Guilty Pour Femme: notes, longevity, and projection at a glance


Gucci Bloom Gucci Guilty Pour Femme


Feel Cool, green white floral Warm, amber fougere floral

Best for Daytime, spring, the office Evenings, fall, date night


## Which is better, Gucci Bloom or Gucci Guilty Pour Femme?


The differentiator here isn’t quality, it’s genre. Bloom is a florist’s-eye white floral kept honest and green for daylight hours. Guilty Pour Femme is a borrowed men’s structure rebuilt into something warmer and more assertive for going out. Reviewers on Scentbird tend to file Bloom under everyday and elegant, and Guilty Pour Femme under date night, which lines up with how each one actually behaves on skin. That gap also shows up in how each one performs in a group setting: Bloom stays polite once it settles, while Guilty Pour Femme’s amber base is the part people are more likely to notice from across a table.


The short answer


Choose Gucci Bloom if you want an honest, linear white floral you can wear anywhere in daylight without a second thought. Choose Gucci Guilty Pour Femme if you want the fougere backbone of a men’s fragrance reworked into something warmer and more assertive for evenings.


Notes on a screen only get you so far with a fragrance this different from itself in either direction, so the next step is wearing each one long enough to catch it through a full day.


Spend real time with it before any bigger commitment.

## Frequently asked questions


What does Gucci Bloom smell like?


Gucci Bloom is a white floral built on tuberose, jasmine, and Rangoon creeper, a flower that changes color as it opens. There is no citrus or fruit introduction, so it reads green, dewy, and slightly powdery from the first spray through the drydown.


What does Gucci Guilty Pour Femme smell like?


Gucci Guilty Pour Femme opens with pink pepper, peach, and mandarin, then moves into a fougere accord built on geranium and lilac before settling into amber, patchouli, and vanilla. It reads warmer and more layered than a typical floral.


What is the main difference between Gucci Bloom and Gucci Guilty?


Gucci Bloom is a linear white floral kept green and fresh throughout, while Gucci Guilty Pour Femme borrows a fougere structure from menswear and warms it with geranium, amber, and patchouli. One stays still, the other changes across three stages.


Which lasts longer, Gucci Bloom or Gucci Guilty Pour Femme?


Both typically run about seven to nine hours on skin. Bloom projects hardest early and then sits close to the skin, while Guilty Pour Femme keeps a warmer amber trail that lingers a bit more noticeably through its final hours.


Is Gucci Bloom or Gucci Guilty Pour Femme better for the office?


Gucci Bloom is the easier office choice because it stays green and light rather than announcing itself. Gucci Guilty Pour Femme’s amber and patchouli base can feel like too much in a small, shared room unless it is applied sparingly.


Can the same person wear both Gucci Bloom and Gucci Guilty Pour Femme?


Yes, and many people do, since the two cover different moods rather than competing for the same one. Bloom suits daytime and warm weather, while Guilty Pour Femme suits evenings and cooler months, so owning both fills out a wider rotation.
